facts.statement: The scientific name of this extinct animal is Dunstanetta johnstoneorum.
The species was described based on a fossil distal left humerus found at the Saint Bathans Fauna site on Home Hills Station.
facts.quote: It was described from fossil material (a distal left humerus) collected from a Saint Bathans Fauna site on Home Hills Station

facts.statement: The genus name Dunstanetta refers to the Dunstan Range, which overlooks the fossil site.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the Dunstan Range, the mountains of which overlook the fossil site

facts.statement: The specific epithet johnstoneorum honors Ann and Euan Johnstone of Home Hills Station.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honours Ann and Euan Johnstone of Home Hills Station

facts.statement: Dunstanetta johnstoneorum is an extinct species of duck from the Miocene of New Zealand.
facts.quote: Dunstanetta johnstoneorum is a genus and species of extinct duck from the Miocene of New Zealand

facts.statement: The genus Dunstanetta belongs to the subfamily Oxyurinae.
The genus Dunstanetta is classified within the family Anatidae.
Fossils of Dunstanetta date to the Early Miocene epoch.
The time range for Dunstanetta is from the Burdigalian to the Langhian, between 18.7 and 15.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Langhian (18.7 to 15.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The fossil material was found in the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group in the Manuherikia River valley of the Central Otago region on New Zealand's South Island.
facts.quote: in the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group, in the Manuherikia River valley in the Central Otago region of the South Island

rejected.statement: The species was described by Worthy and colleagues in 2007.
